findings.title: A filter answer is dropped when a refresh that was already running answers first; the table stays unfiltered under a filtered select and address (hx-sync does not cover this)
findings.repro: Fixed AHM-03 build, 8 alerts of mixed severity. scripts/pw_filter_race.js: trigger a refresh (as an alerts-changed event does), and 100 ms later choose Severity = Medium; every table answer takes 800 ms (slow Pi). The refresh was sent first, so it answers first and replaces #alerts. The filter request was aimed at the old #alerts (htmx resolves hx-target when the request is sent; Pe() returns without swapping when the target has no parent), but its hx-push-url still runs. This also happens without artificial delays whenever a refresh is in flight as the filter changes, for example right after the page loads (the stream sends alerts-changed at once). Same result on the original build: the race was there before this change and is not fixed by it.
findings.evidence: fixed-03: '?status=&severity= sent +12 ms, answered +834 ms' / '?status=&severity=medium sent +164 ms, answered +977 ms' / 'after both answers: {"url":"?status=&severity=medium","select":"medium","rows":["Critical","High","High","High","Medium","Medium","Low","Info"],"refreshUrl":"/?status=&severity="}' and 'after the next refresh:' identical. With the fix: 'rows":["Medium","Medium"],"refreshUrl":"/?status=&severity=medium"'. The earlier late-refresh and refresh-during-refresh checks still pass with the fix.

findings.title: The browser's form restore on Back can defeat the stale-form check and silently undo another analyst's status
findings.repro: Fixed AHM-03 build, scripts/pw_restore.js. Ahmad opens an alert (status New) and goes to /upload. Fiona sets the status to Resolved. Ahmad presses Back and the page is fetched from the server again, not from the HTTP cache. The hidden shown_status is fresh ('resolved'), but Chromium puts the select back to its old value ('new') although he never changed it. He types only his name and saves; the server sees status 'new' != shown 'resolved' and writes it. Today this happens when the cache entry is gone (eviction, DevTools 'Disable cache'). It would happen on every Back if the pages are later sent with Cache-Control: no-store, a likely hardening step; I checked that with an experimental no-store copy and plain goBack().
findings.evidence: FRESH=1 run: 'after Back:   {"select":"new","shown_status":"resolved",...}' / 'he saved his name; stored now: new / Ahmad'. no-store experiment, no routing: the same two lines. With autocomplete="off": 'after Back: {"select":"resolved","shown_status":"resolved"...}' / 'stored now: resolved / Ahmad'. A normal Back from the HTTP cache is protected: 'stored now: resolved / Ahmad'.

+def text_field(value) -> str:
